Bayley - who commuted from Scotland to be at every League match, Pat Lyttle; Snowy - now back in the BL after 10 years; Terry Welsh - our remaining resident Irish Guard;Paul Whitby - who intends to commute from Scotland next season.
Snowy made a welcome return and boosted our field team. We now have four big men capable of beating the best and it was good to see Field Captain John Aska keeping everybody on their toes.

Other winners included Stu Paton (800), Steve Samson (PV) Terry Welsh (HT), Snowy (JT). John Aska did his usual great work organising the field side and surprised himself and everybody else, with his largest javelin throw for some time of 53.84.
Thanks to a second dress rehearsal for Trooping the Colour, we could not call on any of our guards and with Snowy also unavailable we were very weak in the throws.
The other stars on the day were Mark in the P.V. Derek 400, LJ; Snowy SP and the announcer's nightmare!
Derek Williams was at his brilliant best as were Ken, Snowy, Vincent, Mark and sprinters Pat Lyttle and Mike Alleyne. Benny did his usual trick in the B 800 of being last with 200 to go.

John Bicourt won the S/C in 9:05.5 a brilliant run for a 38 year old youngster! Neil Phillips won the 'B' discus as did Snowy in the 'B' shot. A great day with the Bels. still on the up - Div. 3 next year!

But even with Abi and Snowy winning both strings of the discus, the boys from the South Coast won the day. 100m: 3, S.Dominetti 11.9; 1, J.Carr 11.8. 200m: 2, S.Dominetti 23.5; 1, J.Carr 23.8. 400m: 2, D.Winson 53.8; 2, M.Chuter 54.8. 800m: 3, N.Clarke 2:01.2; 2, M.Bowers 2:07.0. 1500m: 4, N.Clarke…
With our throws sorted out by Snowy Brooks and a welcome guest appearance by Mike Small, it was down to the rest of us to do their efforts justice.
Life-member Snowy was our only winner of the evening, although judging from the lack of a recall shot in his 100m, the starter must have been a little short of ammunition.

Snowy was strutting his stuff as normal (in a very nice black one-piece outfit, trimmed with white harlequin side stripes and embellished with a sequin "Snowy" motif) and with our Hercules men scoring well on the field and our Herne Hill men doing likewise in the sprints, the chance of winning the final was there.

Take poor Snowy: he crashed badly at the third barrier in the 400 hurdles and lay on the track stunned until he heard someone call, "Go for it - the Belgrave man's fallen." That was like waving a red rag to a bull.

At least they were spared the troubles that beset the Division 'Fivers'; a broken down mini-bus caused a late arrival at the meeting which had already started, no Snowy due to Wednesday's fall - and a not surprising last place in the match.

We are so strong in the throws and pick up points all over the place in over 50 events thanks to Captain Snowy. Just to level up the race for points, however, we always seem give ourselves the handicap of going into each match with an almost total lack of middle-distance runners.

As mentioned on this page, the late Bill Couzens was jointly responsible for the instigation of our Darts Championship and it was fitting that the 40th competition for the "Pot" was won last December by Bill's colleague in many a field event - Snowy Brooks.
